conflict_synopsis.core_view: BoC energy pass-through hike optionality is the dated closer, and CA-US 5Y cheapened the wrong way after the minutes.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Canadian CPI that shows fuel leaking into underlying inflation, then BoC communications that reprice hike odds.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Trim/median stay near 2 percent, BoC drops the pass-through trigger, or oil collapses and CA-US 5Y makes new lows on US-only backup.
conflict_synopsis.time_horizon: next 1-2 Canadian CPI prints and following BoC window

remit: credible path from mispricing to repricing
stance_summary: Valuation stretch in CA-US 5Y is not the trade; the trade is that BoC minutes just named energy pass-through as the hike trigger and the spread cheapened the wrong way. Own the dated CPI-to-BoC transmission in rates RV, not a catalyst-free fade of rich US yields or a noisy CAD spot.

catalysts: Canadian CPI prints that show energy spreading beyond fuel into trim/median/core
Next BoC deliberation/communications repricing hike odds after the minutes' pass-through language
Further evidence that energy-market shock absorbers remain weak (or fail), keeping WTI/Brent elevated enough to threaten Canadian fuel pass-through

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Duration-matched pay Canada 5Y versus receive US 5Y (CA-US 5Y spread less negative as BoC hike optionality is priced).
expression_comparison.rationale: The discrepancy lives in the common-date CA-US 5Y spread (0th percentile, z about -2.05 on 17 Sep), which is the stretched series the packet flags. USDCAD versus CA-US 2Y is a weak residual (status weak, low r-squared), so spot does not own the rates gap; oil can also move CAD independently of BoC odds. Rates RV is comparably cleaner and is the default under the expression mandate. Spot is the backup, not the primary, because it mixes a policy-repricing view with carry (USD +140bp 2Y over CAD, which opposes short USDCAD) and an undocumented oil beta.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short USDCAD (CAD higher) as the FX expression of a BoC tightening catch-up versus the Fed.

trade.horizon: Next 1-2 Canadian CPI prints and the following BoC communication window
trade.invalidation: Thesis fails if subsequent Canadian CPI keeps CPI-trim and CPI-median near 2 percent with no broadening beyond fuel, or if BoC communications drop the pass-through tightening trigger, or if CA-US 5Y makes new lows on a US-only yield backup rather than Canada failing to catch up. Oil collapsing on the Saudi-Oman workaround would remove the named catalyst even if the spread is still statistically cheap.
trade.mispricing: CA-US 5Y at -124bp is the 0th percentile of the packet's 252-observation window and cheapened another 12bp over five days during the week the BoC minutes put hike optionality on the table. Pricing still treats Canada as a structural laggard to the Fed rather than a conditional hiking candidate. That is a fundamentals-versus-pricing and market-versus-market gap with an identified closer, not a z-score fade of US 5Y (US 5Y is also 99th-percentile rich on 1y history, which is why the expression is relative).
principal_risks: Pass-through never arrives: headline stays energy-heavy while trim/median remain near 2 percent, so the BoC never uses the trigger it named.
Saudi-Oman workaround and any subsequent oil easing cap the energy shock and retire the catalyst.
CA labor deterioration (August employment -42k, cooler wages, unemployment 6.4 percent) keeps the BoC on hold despite energy talk.
US yields outpace Canada if another Fed hike is priced, driving CA-US 5Y more negative; receive-US then loses as an overlay.
Positioning and flow are unavailable; the 17 Sep CA yield decline could be plumbing rather than a policy view.
CA versus US observation dates are not identical (CA 17 Sep, US 18 Sep in some screens); market_state is stale because NZ rates are unavailable.
trade.structure: Duration-matched pay Canada 5Y versus receive US 5Y
trade.thesis: FACT: On 16 Sep the Fed delivered the widely pre-priced 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00 percent. The BoC had already held at 2.25 percent; the Sep 16 minutes said the risk of fuel inflation spreading more broadly had increased and the packet's retained read is that broader energy pass-through is the clearest conditional trigger for renewed BoC tightening. Canada August headline CPI held at 3.0 percent y/y while CPI-trim was 1.9 percent and CPI-median 2.0 percent. Common-date CA-US 5Y was -124bp on 17 Sep (opportunity-monitor percentile 0.0, z -2.05; 5d change -12bp). WTI was 107.02 on 15 Sep (96th percentile, about +24 percent 1m log) and Brent 130.8 (99.6th percentile). Desk thesis: energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse after BoJ hiked to 1.25 percent and BoE held 6-3 with gilt QT. CA Q2 real GDP was +0.8 percent q/q and activity temperature 53.2; CA labor temperature 48.8 with August employment -42k and cooler wages. INFERENCE: Markets are still backsolving a durable BoC hold/relative-easing regime from near-target core and the Sep 2 hold, even though the new information is a named pass-through trigger plus still-elevated oil and a broader G10 tightening impulse. The closing mechanism is sequential Canadian CPI prints that show fuel leaking into underlying inflation, then BoC communications that reprice hike odds; that should lift CA 5Y versus US 5Y (spread less negative). Receive-US is a hedge against global duration, not a US-easing call: the Fed event is largely known information. UNKNOWN: exact next CPI and BoC dates are not in the packet; whether pass-through actually broadens versus stays in fuel; positioning/flow; whether the Saudi-Oman workaround caps oil enough to kill the trigger; CA 17 Sep versus US 18 Sep observation lag.
why_now: BoC minutes (Sep 16 surface) newly named broader energy pass-through as the conditional trigger for renewed tightening after a 2.25 percent hold; known hold needs this new transmission to matter.
CA-US 5Y moved the wrong way into that information: 0th percentile at -124bp, 5d -12bp, 1m -16bp on common dates.
The Fed hike itself is stale as a US catalyst (greater-than-90 percent priced into 16 Sep); residual repricing is Canada's catch-up versus an already-delivered US move.
Physical energy channel is live (WTI 96th percentile, Brent 99.6th; shock-absorbers-weaken headline) even after a Saudi-Oman workaround reduced the extreme supply tail.
Global tightening broadened on 17 Sep (BoJ to 1.25 percent; BoE 6-3 hold plus multi-year gilt unwind), keeping term-rate pressure elevated while Canada remains the policy laggard.
